idiom_name: Ktor install(RequestValidation) plugin + StatusPages error contract
implementation_notes: Ktor models the request pipeline explicitly, and its RequestValidation plugin is the pattern ready-made: install it once, declare `validate<T> { ... }` rules returning ValidationResult.Valid/Invalid for received bodies, and map the raised RequestValidationException to a uniform 400 in StatusPages. Plugins sit between routing and the handler and can be installed globally or per route, replacing a hand-written interceptor chain; ContentNegotiation/kotlinx.serialization parses the body first, so the plugin validates typed objects rather than raw bytes. In Spring-based Kotlin services the JVM realization is Bean Validation with @Valid as in the java file.
pitfalls: The plugin only validates bodies received via call.receive<T>() on covered routes; path/query parameters and uninstalled routes need their own checks - install globally to avoid silent gaps.

Validation runs after deserialization, so malformed or oversized payloads can fail in ContentNegotiation before any validator runs; keep the serialization and validation error paths distinct in StatusPages.
Plugin installation is per Application, not per server instance: a second embeddedServer or test application needs the same installation, otherwise tests validate different behaviour than production.
